claim: The taxonomy requirement `5392cca550c4` states the profile "declares the legal edges — which reference fields a type may carry and what node types they may point at", and both the generate-schemas requirement `ef55248cb3ca` and this bead's own leaf (arch_module_schema.md, composition paragraph) promise that "a project declaring an `endpoint` type gets an `endpoints` array validated exactly as `components` is" — where `components` carries the reference fields `implements` and `uses`. But no leaf specifies how a profile-declared edge whose source is a non-built-in type reaches the composed schema: the composition contract (arch_schema_loader.md compose item, arch_module_schema.md) names only "one array property per module-scoped node type", and S27's expected envelope for the generic type lists only an identity-hash id, a non-empty name and a required content path. The spec is a hole: edge declaration is promised at the requirement level and unspecified at the composition level.
authoritative_source: Requirement `5392cca550c4` (Declare the node taxonomy) is the truth: an edge declaration states which reference fields a type MAY CARRY, so a profile declaring an edge kind with a custom type as its source must yield a composed schema in which nodes of that type can carry the field. The DAG contract in `91270a8a2b57` ("acyclicity over every edge kind the profile declares") and the coverage-chain triples presuppose the same: an edge that no document can legally contain cannot form a cycle or satisfy a chain.
evidence: Implementation resolved the hole in the restrictive direction and pinned it: genericNodeDef (schema/module_compose.go:142-175) emits an `additionalProperties: false` envelope over id/name/description (plus content when required) for every non-built-in type, ComposeModuleSchema and ComposeProjectSchema never read the profile's Edges at all (no reference in either file), and TestFR2_S27_ProfileDeclaredArrayAccepted's "extra field" subtest (schema/module_schema_test.go) asserts that an endpoint carrying any additional field is rejected — a case the spec's S27 does not contain. Consequence: a profile declaring an edge from a custom type passes ProfileLoader validation (edges are checked against declared type names), yet every document in which a node of that type actually carries the declared field fails schema validation. The edge half of `5392cca550c4` is therefore undeliverable for every non-built-in type, and DAG participation or a coverage chain with a custom-type source is unsatisfiable — the two spec halves contradict through the composed schema. Under the default profile nothing exposes this, because the five built-in types resolve to the frame's $defs, which carry their reference fields; every golden acceptance check runs on the default profile.
proposed_fix: Specify edge-field composition in the ModuleSchema/ProjectSchema and SchemaLoader leaves: the composed definition for each declared type gains one property per profile-declared edge kind whose source names that type, validated as identity-hash values; the edge declaration must then also state cardinality (today's built-in kinds are arrays except the scalar preq_id, and the profile's Edge shape currently has no way to say which). Extend S27 with a custom type carrying a declared edge field, and relax the test code's "extra field" pin to reject only fields that are neither envelope nor declared-edge. Alternatively, fold the fix into the forthcoming profile-v2 proposal (declared data fields per type), whose field-declaration mechanism subsumes edge carriage — in that case this report resolves to that proposal rather than to a point fix.
